card.name: Mohobelo
card.tagline: Basotho men's vigorous striding, sliding and leaping dance
card.profile: Mohobelo is the vigorous men's dance of the Basotho of Lesotho, a 'stride, slide and leap' dance marked by high kicks and acrobatic leaps (Music In Africa). Per Music In Africa, in the late 1800s Basotho men guarding outposts in the Maluti Mountains began to add energetic movements and a new style of dancing music, mohobelo, was born in the community of Ha-Molapo in the northern district of Leribe. The music follows a call-and-response pattern in a five-tone scale, the humming 'ho hoba' giving the dance its name; it requires great energy and endurance and is danced mainly in the evening for entertainment (Music In Africa; South Africa Online).
card.insight: Mohobelo travelled to South Africa's gold mines with Basotho migrant labourers in the early 20th century, where inter-mine dance contests produced the European-style brogues-and-bell-bottoms costume still seen at festivals today (Music In Africa).
card.image_significance: The Basotho men's striding/leaping dance. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — Basotho, Lesotho.
